topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, frames the cancer lecture series, and outlines the key learning objectives regarding environmental exposures and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual framework of cancer development as an interplay between endogenous cellular processes, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens contribute to malignancy, illustrated in detail by the epidemiology and etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: DNA Damage and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which specific chemical and physical mutagens damage DNA directly or following xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic drivers of cancer, focusing on how chronic inflammation, promoting agents, and host developmental stages facilitate clonal outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify mutational signatures and evaluate carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk–Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes with a summary of environmental cancer risks and the everyday appraisal of risks against benefits.
